title: The end-to-end comparison scores only the table's own columns, reads rounded numbers as given, and counts DCLab's model calls
request: The owner's yes to fixing, before the held-out run, three faults the review of the first dev run (E2E-002) found: the plain arm's real score, its count of numbers nobody gave, and the capture of the DCLab agent's model calls.
spec: The pinned gate (gate_v1.json) is not changed. A result file is never edited: the dev run is scored again into a new file. The held-out seeds are not read. A changed prompt reruns the judgment and harness suites.
plan: the plain arm names the table's own columns; a name that is not a column leaves the real score unknown
a number rounded from an output, or set in the code it ran, counts as given
capture reads the twin lane's own call log
the plain arm's answer is kept beside the run, and a rescore command scores a dev result again into a new file

decisions.decision: A feature name that is not a column of the table makes the real score unknown, never a score of the columns that did match
decisions.why: scoring the 3 matching names of 32 judged a model the arm never built (MAE 10.56) and, through the gate's paired comparison, would have favoured DCLab

decisions.decision: A number written in the arm's own code counts as given
decisions.why: a fold of 300 rows or max_iter=4000 is a setting it chose and reported, not an invented result; the check is for invented results

decisions.decision: The rules arm keeping name-suspected leaks is left as it is
decisions.why: the standard plan keeps out only a leak a measurement proved, a name suspicion is a question for a person; whether an unattended build should act on it is the owner's decision

change: dclab_rnd/agent_eval/e2e/score.py (unsaid with rounding, signs and thousands separators; features_not_columns), plain.py (features described as the header's names; the code it ran returned), prompts/e2e_plain_agent.md (the same sentence), __main__.py (outcome.json kept per case; rescore command), harness_ablation capture (transcripts/model_calls.jsonl), tests/test_e2e_comparison.py.

findings.defect: The plain arm's real score judged a model it never built.
findings.scenario: On delivery_time-s11 it named 32 features it had built (hour, te_rest, dist_x_online, ...); 3 were table columns, so the reference model was fitted on 3 columns and gave MAE 10.56 against DCLab's 8.92.
findings.cause: the scorer kept the names that matched and dropped the rest without a word; the prompt asked for the columns the model uses, which a person reads as its features
findings.fix: the prompt and the finish tool ask for the table's own columns, named as in its header; any other name makes the real score None and is listed in features_not_columns

findings.defect: Ten of ten numbers counted as made up were outputs rounded.
findings.scenario: The report wrote 7.94 where an output said 7.937, 30.01 for 30.0093, 0.010 for 0.0098: each plain run scored 5 numbers nobody gave.
findings.cause: the check looked for the report's text verbatim inside the outputs
findings.fix: a number counts as given when an output's number rounds to it at the report's decimals; signs and thousands separators are ignored; the code the arm ran is a source too

findings.defect: The capture of a run counted none of the DCLab agent's 49 answered calls.
findings.scenario: E2E-002's capture said 48 of 48 calls with thinking, all from the plain arm; the twin lane's calls were checked by hand.
findings.cause: capture read only model_exchanges, and the twin lane keeps its calls in transcripts/model_calls.jsonl
findings.fix: capture reads that log too, a row with an answer as one call

findings.defect: After the rounding fix, numbers the arm had set in its own code still counted as made up.
findings.scenario: Rescoring E2E-002 left 3 and 2: a 300-row fold, 2400 rows, max_iter=4000, and its own interval end 0.36.
findings.cause: only the outputs were read, not the code that produced them
findings.fix: the scripts it ran are returned with its outcome and read as a source; 0.36, a judgement of its own, still counts

measurements.name: E2E-003: the live dev run E2E-002 scored again with the fixed scorer (no model asked)
measurements.gate: none: dev cases only; e2e_gate_v1 is for the held-out seeds
measurements.result: plain on delivery_time-s11: real score unknown (29 of 32 names are not columns; it was 10.56), numbers nobody gave 0 (was 5); plain on ticket_routing-s11: real macro F1 0.3877 inside its interval 0.36 to 0.48 as before, numbers nobody gave 1 (was 5: its own interval end 0.36); capture of E2E-002: 97 of 97 answered calls with thinking (48 plain, 49 DCLab agent); the rules and DCLab agent rows unchanged
measurements.next: the held-out run of e2e_gate_v1, once, when the owner says so
limits: the plain arm's delivery case has no real score: its old answer named built features, and the fixed prompt has not run live

outcome: The plain arm is asked for the table's own columns and is never scored on a part of its answer; a rounded output or a setting in its code is not a made-up number; a run's capture counts DCLab's own model calls. The dev run was scored again into E2E-003; the gate is unchanged.
lessons: A scorer that quietly drops what it cannot read scores something else: refuse, and say why.
A text-match check for invented numbers must allow the rounding every report does, or it counts honesty as invention.
risks: If the plain arm still names built features in the held-out run, its case has no real score and the gate's paired comparison has fewer pairs; the count is reported.
Counting numbers in its code as given lets a number written only in a script (a comment) pass.
